recommendation: Keep the audit commit. If future work changes active/inactive/resolved meanings, perform that work through THO/UTG terminology governance rather than by reintroducing local core CodeSystem source.
issue_request: FHIR-19634 was Published / Persuasive with Modification for STU3 and asked to update AllergyIntolerance.clinicalStatus CodeSystem definitions: active means currently experiencing or at risk of a reaction, inactive means no longer at risk, and resolved means clinically reassessed by testing or re-exposure and considered no longer present.
initial_application: Commit cccb69d8142e7ec5234dde242ca3da5d556591f5 applied the issue by changing the former core source/allergyintolerance/codesystem-allergyintolerance-clinical.xml definitions. R4 package artifacts retain those corrected definitions, confirming the change reached publication.
additional_context: Current core no longer contains the CodeSystem XML because 5c0494aacfd0b8bd52bc72c587aa89d0a64246f8 removed UTG content from the core build. AllergyIntolerance remains active in source/fhir.ini, and its current value set includes http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/allergyintolerance-clinical. Current THO CodeSystem 1.0.1 carries the FHIR-19634 definitions. Later FHIR-36742 and related Zulip discussion concerned rendering the nested inactive/resolved hierarchy, not changing these definitions; FHIR-28458 added refuted-verification guidance without altering the AllergyIntolerance clinical status CodeSystem.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current FHIR core checkout is correct: it references the external terminology CodeSystem, and that authoritative external artifact already matches the approved issue semantics.
